newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CREDIT OUTLOOK -- Supply and FOMC jitters.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CREDIT OUTLOOK -- Supply and FOMC jitters.

text.p: U.S. debt markets will have a tough week as investors put final touches on their strategies ahead of a key meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy-setting committee on Tuesday, analysts said.
Wall Street experts said prices are likely to stay choppy in the first few days of the week as yield-curve flattening trades and fresh Treasury supply are expected to add volatility to the market.

"I think we can expect a very choppy trade in the first part of the week, especially since it's ahead of the FOMC and we have an auction on Tuesday," said Astrid Adolfson, senior economist at consulting firm MCM MoneyWatch Inc.
The Federal Open Market Committee, the central bank's policy-setting body, will meet on March 25 to decide on whether or not to change the course of monetary policy.
Although the jury remains out on what the Fed will do, analysts said a close look at the U.S. Treasury's yield curve suggests the market is expecting a tightening of monetary policy on Tuesday.
"I think the market has an 80 percent probability on a (Fed) move next Tuesday," said Patrick Dimick, Treasury market strategist at UBS Securities Inc.
A majority of money market analysts seems to believe the Fed will raise the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent.

Analysts said they will pay special attention to the performance of the Treasury's monthly two-year note auction on Tuesday, mainly because the sale's bidding deadline will precede the end of the FOMC meeting.
The auction's deadline is set for 1300 EST/1800 GMT. The outcome of the FOMC meeting is expected to be announced at 1415 EST/1915 GMT.
Analysts said the yield on the two-year note auction is expected to rise from the levels seen in the when-issue trade on Friday as players brace for the possibility of a Fed tightening on Tuesday.
"I think the (two-year) WI has to go back to 6.35 percent before people even consider participating in the auction. And I think it will," Dimick said.
"So you're due for a little more curve flattening through Monday and early Tuesday as this two-year note auction is greeted with a lot of skepticism," Dimick added.
The two-year yield was quoted at 6.3125 percent in late when-issued trade on Friday.
Analysts said the market will also keep an eye on some fresh data next week, including February durable goods, jobless claims for the week of March 22 and consumer confidence for March.
"The market will look back at data after the FOMC is out of the way," said a trader at a U.S. investment bank.
The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was quoted down 3/32 at 95-24/32 to yield 6.96 percent in late Friday trading.
The Fed refrained from open market operations on Friday. Federal funds are seen opening 5.31 percent on Monday.
